verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Timothy the brother,
verses.1:2: to those who are at Colossae, the saints and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you,
verses.1:4: hearing of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love that you have toward all the saints,
verses.1:5: because of the hope that is stored up for you in the heavens, which you heard of in the word of the truth of the gospel,
verses.1:6: which has come to you, just as it is also in the entire world, and is bearing fruit and growing, just as in you, from that day on which you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
verses.1:7: just as you learned from Epaphras, our most beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ Jesus on your behalf,
verses.1:8: who also revealed to us your love in the Spirit.
verses.1:9: For this reason we also, from the day we heard, do not cease praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
verses.1:10: so that you may walk worthily of God, pleasing Him in all things, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
verses.1:11: strengthened with all power according to the might of His splendor, in all patience and forbearance with joy,
verses.1:12: giving thanks to God the Father, who has made us worthy for a share of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
verses.1:13: who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
verses.1:14: in whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins,
verses.1:15: who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
verses.1:16: because in Him all things were created in the heavens and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or authorities; all things have been created through Him and in Him,
verses.1:17: and He is before all, and all things hold together in Him.
verses.1:18: And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in all things He Himself may hold first place,
verses.1:19: because in Him it was well pleasing for all fullness to dwell,
verses.1:20: and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, making peace through the blood of His cross, whether the things on earth or the things in the heavens.
verses.1:21: And although you were once alienated and enemies in mind in evil works,
verses.1:22: yet now He has reconciled you in the body of His flesh through death, to present you holy and unblemished and blameless before Him,
verses.1:23: if indeed you remain in the faith, grounded and steadfast and unmoved from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation that is under heaven, of which I, Paul, was made a minister.
verses.1:24: And I now rejoice in sufferings for you, and fill up the things that are lacking of the sufferings of Christ in my flesh for His body, which is the church,
verses.1:25: of which I was made a minister according to the stewardship of God that was given to me for you, so that I may fulfill the word of God,
verses.1:26: the mystery that was hidden from ages and generations, but has now been revealed to His saints,
verses.1:27: to whom God willed to make known the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ, in you the hope of glory,
verses.1:28: whom we proclaim, correcting every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus;
verses.1:29: in which I also labor, striving according to His working, which He works in me with power.
verses.2:1: For I want you to know what concern I have for you, and for those who are at Laodicea, and for all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
verses.2:2: so that their hearts may be comforted, being instructed in love, and to all the riches of the fullness of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ Jesus,
verses.2:3: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
verses.2:4: Now I say this so that no one may deceive you by loftiness of words.
verses.2:5: For even though I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing and seeing your order and the steadfastness of your faith that is in Christ.
verses.2:6: Therefore, just as you received Jesus Christ the Lord, walk in Him,
verses.2:7: rooted and built up in Him, and established in faith, just as you also learned, abounding in Him in thanksgiving.
verses.2:8: See to it that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ,
verses.2:9: because in Him all the fullness of divinity dwells bodily,
verses.2:10: and you have been filled in Him, who is the head of every principality and authority,
verses.2:11: in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, but in the circumcision of Christ,
verses.2:12: buried together with Him in baptism, in which you also rose again through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from the dead.
verses.2:13: And when you were dead in transgressions and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made you alive together with Him, forgiving you all transgressions,
verses.2:14: blotting out the handwritten record of the decree that was against us, which was contrary to us; and He took it out of the way, fastening it to the cross,
verses.2:15: and stripping the principalities and authorities, He exposed them boldly, openly triumphing over them in Himself.
verses.2:16: Therefore let no one judge you in food or in drink, or in respect to a feast day, or a new moon, or Sabbaths,
verses.2:17: which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ's.
verses.2:18: Let no one lead you astray, delighting in humility and the worship of angels, walking in things that he has not seen, puffed up in vain by the mind of his flesh,
verses.2:19: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and built together through ligaments and joints, grows into the increase of God.
verses.2:20: If therefore you died with Christ from the elements of this world, why do you still make decrees as though living in the world?
verses.2:21: "Do not touch, nor taste, nor handle,"
verses.2:22: which are all for destruction by their very use, according to the precepts and teachings of men,
verses.2:23: which indeed have a semblance of wisdom in superstition and humility and in not sparing the body, not in any honor for the filling of the flesh.
verses.3:1: Therefore, if you have risen together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, sitting at God's right hand.
verses.3:2: Keep your minds set on the things that are above, not on the things on the earth.
verses.3:3: For you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
verses.3:4: When Christ, your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
verses.3:5: Put to death, therefore, your members that are on the earth: fornication, impurity, lust, evil desire, and greed, which is servitude to idols.
verses.3:6: On account of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of unbelief.
verses.3:7: In these things you also once walked, when you were living in them.
verses.3:8: But now, you too, lay aside all of them: wrath, indignation, malice, blasphemy, foul speech from your mouth.
verses.3:9: Do not lie to one another, stripping off the old man with his deeds,
verses.3:10: and clothing yourselves with the new one, who is being renewed into knowledge according to the image of Him who created him,
verses.3:11: where there is not Gentile and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian and Scythian, slave and free; but Christ is all things, and in all.
verses.3:12: Clothe yourselves, therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, with a heart of mercy, kindness, humility, modesty, patience,
verses.3:13: bearing with one another and forgiving one another if anyone has a complaint against another; just as the Lord also forgave you, so too must you.
verses.3:14: Over all these things, however, have love, which is the bond of perfection;
verses.3:15: and let the peace of Christ exult in your hearts, in which you were also called in one body; and be thankful.
verses.3:16: Let the word of Christ dwell abundantly in you, in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing in grace to God in your hearts.
verses.3:17: Everything, whatever you do in word or in deed, do all things in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father through Him.
verses.3:18: Wives, be submissive to your husbands, as is proper, in the Lord.
verses.3:19: Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter toward them.
verses.3:20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is pleasing in the Lord.
verses.3:21: Fathers, do not provoke your children to indignation, so that they do not become disheartened.
verses.3:22: Slaves, obey your masters in the flesh in all things, not serving for the eye, as if pleasing people, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
verses.3:23: Whatever you do, work from the heart, as for the Lord and not for people,
verses.3:24: knowing that you will receive the reward of the inheritance from the Lord. Serve the Lord Christ.
verses.3:25: For the one who does wrong will receive back what he has done unjustly, and there is no partiality with God.
verses.4:1: Masters, render to your slaves what is just and fair, knowing that you have a Master in heaven as well.
verses.4:2: Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving,
verses.4:3: praying at the same time for us as well, that God may open to us a door for the word to speak the mystery of Christ (on account of which I am also bound),
verses.4:4: so that I may make it manifest in the way I ought to speak.
verses.4:5: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.
verses.4:6: Let your speech always be in grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to respond to each one.
verses.4:7: Tychicus, the dearly loved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will make known to you all things concerning me,
verses.4:8: whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, that he may know the things concerning you and comfort your hearts,
verses.4:9: with Onesimus, the dearly loved and faithful brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all things that are taking place here.
verses.4:10: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you have received instructions: if he comes to you, welcome him),
verses.4:11: and Jesus, who is called Justus. They are of the circumcision; these alone are my helpers in the kingdom of God, who have been a consolation to me.
verses.4:12: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you, always earnestly concerned for you in prayers, so that you may stand perfect and full in all the will of God.
verses.4:13: For I testify for him that he has great labor for you, and for those who are in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
verses.4:14: Luke, the dearly loved physician, and Demas greet you.
verses.4:15: Greet the brothers who are in Laodicea, and Nympha, and the church that is in her house.
verses.4:16: And when this letter has been read among you, see to it that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you yourselves read the one that belongs to the Laodiceans.
verses.4:17: And say to Archippus, "See to the ministry that you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it."
verses.4:18: The greeting is in my own hand, Paul's. Be mindful of my chains. Grace be with you. Amen.

notes.1:3: In the Clementine Vulgate, the greeting 'Grace to you and peace...' opens verse 3 rather than closing verse 2, and includes 'and the Lord Jesus Christ,' which is absent from critical Greek editions.
notes.1:10: The Vulgate reads 'digne Deo' ('worthily of God'), whereas the Greek manuscripts read 'worthy of the Lord.'
notes.1:14: The Vulgate includes 'per sanguinem ejus' ('through His blood'), matching the Byzantine Greek tradition (cf. Eph 1:7) rather than critical Greek editions.
notes.1:16: The Vulgate ends the verse with ablative 'in ipso' ('in Him'), differing from Greek 'eis auton' ('for/toward Him').
notes.1:27: Where verse 26 uses 'mysterium' ('mystery'), the Vulgate switches here to 'sacramentum' ('sacrament,' in the patristic sense of a sacred mystery or hidden divine plan), both rendering the same Greek word.
notes.2:2: The Vulgate reads 'instructi in caritate' ('instructed in love') rather than Greek 'knit together in love,' and reads 'Dei Patris et Christi Jesu' ('of God the Father and of Christ Jesus') where critical Greek editions read 'of God, Christ.'
notes.2:8: The Vulgate translates Greek 'sylagogon' ('taking captive') as 'decipiat' ('deceives'), using the same verb as in verse 4.
notes.2:18: The Vulgate renders Greek 'katabrabeueto' ('disqualify') as 'seducat' ('lead astray'), and reads 'quae non vidit ambulans' ('walking in things that he has not seen'), preserving the negative 'non' absent from critical Greek editions.
notes.2:20: The Vulgate uses the active verb 'decernitis' ('you make decrees') rather than the Greek middle/passive ('you submit to decrees'), and adds 'hujus' ('of this world').
notes.2:23: The Vulgate renders Greek 'ethelothreskia' ('self-made religion') as 'superstitione' ('superstition'), and translates the notoriously difficult closing clause literally as 'non in honore aliquo ad saturitatem carnis' ('not in any honor for the filling of the flesh').
notes.3:6: The Vulgate includes the phrase "upon the sons of unbelief" (super filios incredulitatis), which is omitted in some early Greek manuscripts; where present in Greek, the noun means "disobedience" rather than the Vulgate's "unbelief."
notes.3:14: The Vulgate supplies the explicit imperative verb "have" (habete), whereas the Greek text omits a verb here and relies on "put on" carried over from verse 12.
notes.3:15: The Vulgate reads "exult" (exsultet) rather than the Greek "rule" or "act as umpire," and uses the ablative "in which" (in qua) rather than the Greek "to which."
notes.3:24: Latin servite is unambiguously imperative ("Serve the Lord Christ"), whereas the corresponding Greek form can be read as either imperative or indicative ("You are serving the Lord Christ").
notes.3:25: The Vulgate adds "with God" (apud Deum) at the end of the verse, a phrase absent from the Greek text here.
notes.4:8: The Vulgate reads "that he may know the things concerning you" (ut cognoscat quæ circa vos sunt), agreeing with one Greek manuscript tradition against another that reads "that you may know how we are."
notes.4:12: The Vulgate renders the Greek participle meaning "struggling" as "earnestly concerned" (sollicitus) and reads "full" (pleni), reflecting a Greek variant meaning "filled" rather than "fully assured."
notes.4:15: Latin Nympham and the pronoun ejus are grammatically ambiguous in gender and may refer either to a woman ("Nympha... her house") or to a man ("Nymphas... his house").
notes.4:16: The Vulgate reads "the one that belongs to the Laodiceans" (eam, quæ Laodicensium est), a possessive genitive differing from the Greek phrasing "the letter from Laodicea."
notes.4:18: The Vulgate concludes with "Amen," matching the traditional Greek text, though it is omitted in many early Greek manuscripts.
